name: orbit_agent_invoke
description: Submit an asynchronous agent invocation for exploration or debugging and return its run ID, or wait for its answer with `wait_seconds`. Queued submissions include `queued: true`, a one-based `queue_position` and a warning. An operator's invocation runs on the host outside Orbit's filesystem sandbox, as the same OS user as Orbit, so it can reach anything that user can; it is admitted per invocation and requires operator capability — the same test for a session that arrived over SSH as for a local one. An implement or review-repair agent may instead delegate a read-only question when `workflow.explore.enabled` is on: it gets a sandboxed explorer from the explorer crew pool that reads its own worktree, cannot write or change Orbit state, and is bounded by per-run call, concurrency, timeout and answer-size budgets; every other agent is refused, and a refusal never stops the caller's run. Track it with `orbit_workflow_run_show`: `agent_invocation.answer` carries the agent's summary, findings, next_steps, any other result fields and its bounded final message, and `agent_invocation.progress` its latest message and last activity while it runs. Read the complete output with `orbit run logs <RUN_ID>` and stop it with `orbit run cancel <RUN_ID>`. It changes no task, opens no pull request, and dispatches nothing.

prompt.description: What to investigate. The invoked agent reports back; it makes no Orbit task, lifecycle, commit, or pull-request change. An explorer lists the paths it read in `answer.paths_read`.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory the agent starts in. Must exist and be inside this workspace's checkout or a linked worktree under `.orbit/state/worktrees/`; it is never inferred from the caller. An explorer's must be inside the calling run's own worktree.

crew.description: Configured crew selecting the provider, model, and reasoning effort. Defaults to the workspace's default crew. An explorer's must be in `workflow.purpose_crews.explorer`, which it is drawn from when omitted.

timeout_seconds.description: Provider wall-clock bound in seconds, excluding queue time. Defaults to 1800; must be from 1 to 7200, the activity's enforced ceiling. An explorer defaults to, and may not exceed, `workflow.explore.timeout_seconds`.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds (integer from 0 to 600). Returns `answer` and `agent_invocation` if finished; otherwise returns the run ID and actual state so you can keep observing it. The deadline never cancels the run. Omit for an asynchronous submission.

idempotency_key.description: Retry handle. A resubmission carrying a key a recent submission already used resolves that run instead of starting a second agent.

provider_sandbox.description: Per-invocation inner-sandbox override for the selected crew's provider (Codex: `read-only`, `workspace-write`, or `danger-full-access`). Tightens or names the provider sandbox for this run only; values the provider does not support are refused. The submission result reports the effective mode as `provider:mode`. Operator invocations only: an explorer is always read-only.

name: orbit_agents_scorecard
description: Rank one agent role's crews and models over the window: weighted outcome rates per 100 units of work, then pulled down toward the fleet average when above it. Implementers start at 100 and score actual counts against fleet expectations for the same tier mix; tasks tagged no-diff-expected when an attempt was admitted are not implementer work and count nowhere on that scorecard. Other roles sum weighted actual rates. Rows below the minimum support are listed last without a rank; a role whose terms are not computed yet answers status not_computed with its terms and no rows. With by_type, implementers instead return one cell per (crew, model, tier, type) with n, raw, crew_mean and score, plus the type list used. With shadow as well, implementers instead return each crew's draw count and its static, drawn and would-be share per pool and type over the window; draws with no performance record are counted separately as static. With per_task, implementers instead return one row per implemented task with its crew, model, tier, configured type, tags, context-file selectors and path prefixes and per-term counts, plus the type list used. Calls without those switches keep this ranking. Scans the workspace once per call (cache_ttl_seconds 0), except the shadow report, which reads recorded draws only. The payload the dashboard's Agents view reads.

role.description: The agent role to score: orchestrators, implementers, reviewers or pilots.

window.description: Counts work in this period ending now: 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d or all (served as 90d, the scan's reach). Default: 30d.

min_support.description: Units of the role's work a row needs before it is ranked, at least 1; rows below it are listed last without a rank. Default: 10.

by_type.description: Split implementers into (crew, model, tier, type) cells using workflow.crew_performance_types, with two-level shrinkage; implementers only.

shadow.description: For implementers with by_type, report each crew's static, drawn and would-be share from recorded draws instead of the cell matrix. Draws without a performance record are counted separately as static.

per_task.description: Export one row per implemented task for offline analysis, with its crew, model, tier, configured type, tags, context-file path prefixes and per-term counts; implementers only, and not with by_type or shadow.

name: orbit_decision_submit
description: Submit a human's answer to one open decision request through a registered decision channel. Governed: callable only by the plugin the channel is bound to (through its callback session) or by the operator testing a channel — never by an agent session. Core verifies the channel is registered and unrevoked, the request is still open against its binding, the answer is allowed, and the per-request token (single-use, expiring with the request, keyed to the channel's current key epoch). Only then is the answer applied in core as the registered human, with the channel and the token fingerprint recorded as provenance. Every refusal (channel_not_registered, channel_revoked, caller_not_allowed, sender_not_allowed, authentication_failed, token_invalid, token_consumed, request_expired, request_superseded, answer_not_allowed, request_not_found) applies nothing; a parse-level refusal does not consume the token.

answer.description: The human's chosen answer id, one of the request's allowed answers. An empty answer is refused as unparseable.

token.description: The per-request single-use token minted for this request under the channel key. Core verifies it; presenting it never reveals it back.

note.description: Evidence or note kept with the answer. A pilot-admission `evaluated` answer uses it as its evidence and is refused without one.

sender.description: The transport sender the submission presents as evidence, checked against the channel's sender allowlist when the channel has one.

auth_results.description: The raw Authentication-Results header the transport forwards as evidence. When present, core requires dkim=pass and spf=pass and refuses on dmarc=fail.

name: orbit_task_artifact_get
description: Read one stored task artifact by owning task ID and artifact path. Returns `media_type`, `size`, and the bytes: UTF-8 text as `content`, and everything else as base64 in `content_base64`. Supported raster images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) whose bytes match their declared type are additionally returned as a viewable image on transports that carry image content, so a multimodal client can inspect a stored visual reference directly. SVG, HTML, and any payload whose bytes contradict its media type are returned as opaque base64 and are never rendered. List available artifacts first with `orbit_task_show` and `field: "artifacts"`; payloads are fetched only through this call. Reads are bounded to 1048576 bytes.

name: orbit_task_block_triage
description: Triage escalated blocks. `candidates` lists every blocked task with whether its current block episode awaits triage: its final-recovery decision escalated, or it has none and the backstop will never decide it; an episode already triaged or touched by a human after the block is excluded. Each other action records one decision on a qualifying episode, as one task comment plus a history marker, and refuses any other episode. `requeue` returns the task to the backlog as a final-recovery requeue, counted against the shared final-recovery requeue bound (2 per 24 hours): past the bound, for a task tagged security or security-review, or for a run another machine executed, it is recorded as refused and the task stays blocked; when the count cannot be read nothing is written. `propose` records the quoted blocker, two or three options with consequences and ready-to-apply replacement text, and a recommendation, and changes nothing else. `report` records the human action and changes nothing else. Never completes, rejects or archives a task. With `subject` `pilot_warning`, the same actions read `proposed` tasks whose latest task-pilot assessment holds promotion on warning findings instead: `candidates` lists each held assessment not yet triaged and without an operator decision, quoting its holding findings; `propose` and `report` record one comment quoting those findings plus a `pilot_warning_triaged` history marker that excludes the assessment afterwards, and refuse a task that no longer qualifies; `requeue` is refused. A pilot warning triage never approves, promotes, clears a hold or edits any other task field. A decision on a task a live escalation triage run holds must carry that run's inspection proof: its pinned `source_revision` with `observed_revision` and `observed_tree` read from the inspection checkout (`git rev-parse HEAD` and `git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}'`), or, for a run in a non-Git workspace, `source_revision` null and no observed values. The observed pair is checked against the pinned revision's tree, and a missing or mismatched proof records nothing. A proof passed on any other decision is checked the same way.

subject.description: what is triaged: block (default), a blocked task's block episode; pilot_warning, a proposed task's pilot warning hold

blocker.description: block requeue, propose, report: the escalation reason, quoted in the comment; pilot_warning quotes the holding findings itself and refuses it

reason.description: requeue: the repair applied and why the task can run again; report: the specific action only a human can take

name: orbit_workflow_auto
description: Observe workspace auto-drain readiness, start a bounded window, stop admissions while preserving admitted workers (or, with force, stop those workers too), or resize a running drain's worker limit. Resize keeps the run ID, deadline, completion authorization and dispatched children; a lower limit only stops new admissions and cancels nothing. Requires trusted operator authority and an explicit workspace. Start is not retry-safe: reconcile readiness and runs after a lost reply before another submission.

for_seconds.description: Required for start: window length in seconds, 1 through 86400 (24 hours)

auto_concurrency.description: Start only: off, shadow or enforce for this local drain. Omitted captures machine.auto_concurrency.mode. Retained on resume/restart; changes no configuration. Unsupported for pull drains

concurrency.description: Worker limit, positive u32. Optional for start (omitted uses runtime default); required for resize. Status previews this ceiling; omitted uses the live local drain, then live pull drain, then default. The drain's only ceiling: delivery jobs impose none of their own

task.description: Status only: one task ID or a list to explain instead of the bounded backlog

limit.description: Status only: maximum tasks to explain, including an explicit selection (1-500; default 50)

allow_crew.description: Status only: configured crews to evaluate; omitted uses the live drain's restriction, if any

id.description: Resize only: auto- or pull-drain run ID. Omitted targets the workspace's one live drain; refused when none or several are live

if_revision.description: Resize only: apply only if the run's worker limit is still at this revision, so a concurrent change is reported rather than overwritten

reason.description: Resize only: note recorded with the change

complete.description: Start only: explicitly authorize automatic completion for all tasks admitted by this window; default false keeps review. Does not approve proposed tasks

review.description: Start only: add this review layer before landing (before-pr or before-landing) to the window when workspace policy applies none; every task it admits inherits it. The layer policy already applies is accepted unchanged; the other layer, a workspace that sets neither workflow.purpose_crews.pre_landing_review nor workflow.purpose_crews.review and a workspace that delivers locally are refused. It can only add review. Omitted keeps workspace policy

approve_proposed.description: Start only: each pass pilots qualifying proposed tasks (tagged no-diff-expected, or with context_files and an assessed complexity) and approves into backlog those with no duplicate, already-landed, conflict or warning finding, including tasks filed during the window. Tasks tagged no-auto-approve are never approved. Others stay proposed; status reports approved and held counts. Default false

force.description: Stop only: also cancel each live drain and stop its in-flight work. A pull drain's claimed leaves are stopped and their tasks return to the owner's backlog with a comment; a local drain's task runs are cancelled. A leaf that cannot be confirmed stopped keeps its claim and fails the call. Default false stops admissions only

claim_token.description: Workspace claim token when held by another operator

workspace.description: Exact selector returned by workspace discovery. No implicit destination.

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (codex, claude, gemini, grok, or muse); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

name: orbit_workflow_run_list
description: List durable workflow runs newest-first with optional bounded filters. Requires operator capability; agent sessions are refused.

limit.description: Maximum runs to return (default 25; values above 200 are rejected).

since.description: Optional RFC 3339 lower bound for run creation time.

view.description: bounded: bounded metadata, explicit workspace, pagination and display truncation. Omit for the existing full-record response.

include_catalog.description: Bounded view only: include a paginated no-input job catalog with last-run metadata alongside runs

workspace.description: Workspace selector for the authoritative server: a registered workspace name, a logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or an absolute path registered on that server. Optional in this session, which is already bound to a workspace — by `orbit mcp serve --workspace` at launch or `_meta.orbit.workspace` at initialize. Pass it to address a different registered workspace; never inferred from the server process cwd.

name: orbit_workflow_run_resume
description: Resume a terminal resumable workflow run as a new linked run, or explicitly authorize review-only same-PR source repair of an eligible owner-local publication, including successful publication with unmet acceptance. Requires operator capability; agent sessions are refused.

claim_token.description: Token for this workspace's exclusive claim, required when another operator holds one. Falls back to `ORBIT_WORKSPACE_CLAIM_TOKEN`.

source_repair.description: Explicit operator recovery of an eligible stopped owner-local publication. Inspect: {action: inspect, task_id} returns binding, review and policy_digest. Submit: {action: submit, task_id, request_key, binding, diagnosis}; successful-publication rework also requires unmet_acceptance evidence and the inspected current policy_digest. Supply the exact binding object. Diagnosis and unmet_acceptance accept 1-32768 bytes each. Captures current review and workflow.required_validation_commands: configured commands require fresh candidate evidence; an empty list records skipped_no_required_commands, not a passing check, and does not waive configured review or hosted required checks. Reuses the original PR; grants no completion, merge or auto-fix authority.

The answer contains summary, findings, next steps, and extra result fields; stdout blob references retain the complete provider output. Requires operator capability; agent sessions are refused.

name: orbit_workflow_ship
description: Submit explicit tasks to the review-only ship workflow and return its durable run ID. This MCP tool does not accept completion authorization; an authorized operator on the owning host can use `orbit run ship <task-id> --complete`.

task_ids.description: Explicit task IDs to ship; at least one is required.

mode.description: Optional ship mode (`pr` or `local`); defaults to workspace configuration.

allowed_crews.description: Optional configured crews this explicit shipment may dispatch; excluded crews are rejected before provider invocation.

review.description: Optional review layer before landing (`before-pr` or `before-landing`) this run adds when workspace policy applies none. The layer policy already applies is accepted unchanged; the other layer, a workspace that sets neither workflow.purpose_crews.pre_landing_review nor workflow.purpose_crews.review and local-only delivery are refused before the run starts. It can only add review. Omitted keeps workspace policy.

name: orbit_workspace_list
description: List active workspaces with a checkout registered on this machine, optionally with each one's configured crews.

include.description: Optional extra detail per workspace row. `crews` adds the workspace's effective configured crews and default crew as `crews`, read on the machine that holds the checkout, or `crews_error` when its configuration cannot be read.
